column1: # Figure 2D source. Shift in median transferred pseudotime, mutant minus wild type,
# for each cell class mapped onto its externally-defined reference trajectory.
# TEST: two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum on per-cell transferred pseudotime (mutant vs
#   wild-type cells of that class), Benjamini-Hochberg across the 9 classes.
# SYMBOL RULE. The panel carries no significance markers. A point is FILLED when
#   q < 0.05 and open otherwise. 5 of 9 classes are filled.
# TWO CRITERIA AGREE. The previous version of this panel marked points by whether
#   an equal-N resampling interval excluded zero. That criterion and the FDR test
#   classify all 8 classes for which both are available IDENTICALLY - the five
#   filled classes have both q < 0.05 and a resampling interval excluding zero,
#   and the three open classes fail both. Cycling RG has no published resampling
#   interval and is open on the FDR test alone (q = 0.87).
# CYCLING RG. This row appears in the panel but had no per-class summary table in
#   the analysis outputs; it was recomputed here from the mapped cell table
#   09b_dorsal_rg_ipc_exc_mapped_table.csv. As a check, the same recomputation
#   reproduced the published Wilcoxon P for all six classes that do have one
#   (deep-layer EN 6.90e-27, upper-layer EN 1.86e-46, immature astrocytes
#   6.17e-02, LGE-IN precursors 7.91e-01, MGE 9.48e-14, CGE 1.27e-02).
# UNIT OF ANALYSIS. Cells are treated as independent observations. The study has
#   one library per genotype, so cells are pseudoreplicates and these P-values
#   describe how reliably the two libraries differ, not the genotypes.
# ci_low/high are the equal-N resampling interval on the delta median, carried
#   over from the original analysis. They bound sampling-depth instability, not
#   between-animal variation.
